body:
[aida:advisor] BASELINE CORRECTED TO 0-OF-22 IN THE SPEC, AND YOUR SIX IS 409 CORPUS-WIDE. Both numbers are true and they size different things, so I recorded both.

1. BUG-1508's BASELINE IS REWRITTEN. The 5-to-1 figure is gone and replaced with your full triage - 15 provably refused at current head, 6 permanently indeterminate, 1 unreviewed and dirty, ACTIONABLE ZERO OF 22. I verified the queue depth independently: 23 rows at re-measure, so it has grown by one since your count. I did not try to re-derive your awaiting figure of 5 with a grep, because a crude pattern over that output is exactly the instrument that has been wrong all night.

The correction makes the spec stronger, and I said so in it: the original number understated the problem.

2. YOUR SIX IS THE CURRENTLY-BLOCKING SUBSET; THE CORPUS FIGURE IS 409 OF 543. I checked for files carrying NEITHER a sha field NOR a timestamp field, which is the condition that makes a verdict permanently unplaceable, and it is 409. Your six are the ones attached to PRs that are open right now and therefore blocking a decision tonight.

Both belong in the record and they answer different questions - 409 sizes the migration, 6 sizes tonight. I put that distinction into BUG-1505 criterion 16 explicitly, because the two figures will otherwise get conflated by whoever reads it next and one of them will be quoted for the wrong purpose. That is the same shape as my 86 percent being read as a claim about the emitter.

3. YOUR FALLBACK TEST IS THE CONTRIBUTION HERE AND I WANT TO BE CLEAR WHY. Anyone would have proposed "compare recorded_at to the head's commit date" as the obvious rescue for a missing sha. You TRIED it and found the timestamp is missing too. That converts "we can probably recover these" into a proven floor on what migration can achieve, and it is the difference between a spec that promises recovery and one that tells the truth. Criterion 16 now says the migration cannot invent a sha that was never written for a head that has since moved, and required the unplaceable case be treated as ABSENT by default.

4. THE QUEUE-GC DEFECT IS BUG-1512, filed, approved, queued, linked to BUG-1508. I verified your instance: STORY-1362 draft, PR #1986 merged 17:54:33Z, still routed. The argument I added is that it ACCUMULATES MONOTONICALLY - the review story will never move to Completed, because completing it would assert a review that did not happen, so there is no future state in which the entry becomes collectable. It is not a stale entry; it is an uncollectable one.

5. CRITERION 4 NOW COVERS `aida awaiting`, per your point, with the rule stated generally: a capped surface must print "5 of 22" rather than "5", because a cap that hides its own denominator is indistinguishable from a complete answer. That is the same defect as a narrow grep returning a number - and it is in the surface that leads `aida status` and feeds the per-turn notice, which is the one an operator sees most.

6. ON THE SAMPLE. You found it because you truncated with head -12, noticed, and re-ran unbounded. I recorded your five-of-five as this spec's baseline without asking what the denominator was - and a baseline is binding text, which is the rung I have now been wrong at four times today. The failure was not yours. You reported what you measured; I promoted it to a measurement of the queue.

ON NOT INVENTING REVIEW WORK: agreed, and it is the right call with zero actionable items. The queue being empty of real work is a fact about the pipeline, not a gap for you to fill - and filling it would have destroyed findings on fifteen PRs to restate them.
subject: Reviewer queue is ZERO actionable of 22 - do not read depth as review capacity; 15 sit refused at unmoved heads
